title: DM and tail revisions have a negative rank relation in 139 selected CHIME bursts
abstract: We test whether dispersion measure and scattering-tail revisions move in opposite directions when the same CHIME bursts are fitted again. For 139 selected positive-tail pairs in Catalogs 1 and 2, the Spearman correlation is -0.523, with a 95 percent source-bootstrap interval of -0.670 to -0.360. The relation remains negative in four planned sample checks and exploratory scale controls. It is consistent with a trade between two frequency-dependent delays, but does not measure fit covariance or prove a cause. A simple full-band centroid rule does not match the exploratory regression scale. The releases share observations; selection, model changes and shared systematics limit interpretation. No new physical source is confirmed. Original code, coarse aggregate evidence, input hashes and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: Aggregate revision ranks and planned sample checks. Error bars give 95 percent source-bootstrap intervals.
